mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about drawing ray diagrams for a convex lens reflects a common misconception?

options.A: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focal point after refraction.
options.B: A ray passing through the optical centre of the lens continues in a straight line without deviation.
options.C: A ray passing through the focal point emerges parallel to the principal axis after refraction.
options.D: A ray passing through the centre of the lens bends towards the principal axis after refraction.

mcqs.answer: A ray passing through the centre of the lens bends towards the principal axis after refraction.
mcqs.explanation: Option D is a misconception; a ray that passes through the optical centre of a thin lens does not change direction. Options A, B and C correctly describe the three principal rays used in lens diagrams, so they are not misconceptions.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 2f (twice the focal length) in front of a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. What is the nature and position of the image formed?

options.A: Real, inverted, at 20 cm on the opposite side of the lens
options.B: Real, inverted, at 5 cm on the opposite side of the lens
options.C: Virtual, upright, at 20 cm on the same side of the lens
options.D: Virtual, upright, at 5 cm on the same side of the lens

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, at 20 cm on the opposite side of the lens
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, with f = 10 cm and u = -20 cm, we get 1/v = 1/10 - 1/20 = 1/20, so v = +20 cm. Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side, and because the object is beyond f, the image is inverted.

mcqs.question: Which pair of statements correctly distinguishes a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.A: A convex lens diverges light, while a concave lens converges light.
options.B: A convex lens has a real focus, whereas a concave lens has a virtual focus.
options.C: Both lenses produce real, inverted images for objects placed beyond 2f.
options.D: Both lenses have the same sign for focal length.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens has a real focus, whereas a concave lens has a virtual focus.
mcqs.explanation: Convex (converging) lenses bring parallel rays to a real focus on the principal axis; concave (diverging) lenses cause parallel rays to appear to diverge from a virtual focus on the same side as the object. Option A reverses the behavior, C is false for concave lenses, and D is false because their focal lengths have opposite signs.

mcqs.question: In a thin lens, the point through which a ray passes without any deviation is called the:
mcqs.explanation: The optical centre (also called the geometric centre) of a thin lens is the point where an incident ray continues in a straight line without being refracted. The principal focus is where parallel rays converge, the focal point is another term for principal focus, and the principal axis is the line passing through the centre and the foci.

mcqs.question: The point on the principal axis of a convex lens where parallel rays converge after refraction is known as the:
mcqs.explanation: Parallel rays incident on a convex lens meet at the principal focus after refraction. The optical centre is where rays pass undeviated, focal length is the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus, and the vertex is the geometric centre of the lens surface.

mcqs.question: The distance between the optical centre of a thin lens and its principal focus is called the:
mcqs.explanation: Focal length (f) is defined as the distance from the optical centre (or principal plane) of a thin lens to its principal focus. Radius of curvature relates to the curvature of the lens surface, the principal axis is the line through the centre, and lens thickness is a separate dimension.

mcqs.question: When drawing a ray diagram for a thin convex lens, which three principal rays are conventionally used?

options.A: Ray parallel to principal axis, ray through centre, ray through focal point
options.B: Ray through centre, ray parallel to axis, ray through twice focal length
options.C: Ray through focal point, ray parallel to axis, ray reflected from lens surface
options.D: Ray through vertex, ray parallel to axis, ray through centre

mcqs.answer: Ray parallel to principal axis, ray through centre, ray through focal point
mcqs.explanation: The three standard rays for a convex lens are: (1) a ray parallel to the principal axis that passes through the principal focus after refraction, (2) a ray through the optical centre that continues undeviated, and (3) a ray passing through the principal focus that emerges parallel to the principal axis. The other options mix incorrect or irrelevant rays.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 5 cm in front of a thin concave lens of focal length -15 cm. Where is the image formed?

options.A: 7.5 cm on the same side as the object, virtual, upright
options.B: 7.5 cm on the opposite side, real, inverted
options.C: 3.75 cm on the same side as the object, virtual, upright

mcqs.answer: 3.75 cm on the same side as the object, virtual, upright
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u with f = -15 cm and u = -5 cm, we get 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = -1/15 + 1/5 = -1/15 + 3/15 = 2/15, so v = 15/2 = 7.5 cm. However, sign convention for concave lenses gives a virtual image on the same side as the object; the correct calculation yields v = -3.75 cm, indicating the image is 3.75 cm in front of the lens, virtual and upright. Option C matches this result.
